controlled_by: The Geng family. Master Geng Su, an official, died some weeks ago. Steward Pei holds the gate. The elder son is on the road from Longxi.
description: Fourth ward east of the West Market, three doors along from the ward gate. A family with a name and a salary. Retiled expensively about fifteen years ago, untouched since. Weeds at the base of the east wall where a gardener used to be.
name: The Geng house
observed_not_explained: Undyed hemp at the gate posts, weathered grey along the folds. Weeks old.
The burial is delayed. Stated reason: a son travelling back from a provincial post in Longxi.
Four liang of musk delivered every ninth day, ongoing.
The dead man's silk robe went out to a seamstress to be cut down before he is in the ground. (Plausibly explained: the household has lost three servants since the death and is short of money.)
The physician who attends arrives and leaves empty-handed. No case, no boy. Stays about two hours. Three visits since the death.
No physician was called on the night Geng Su died. Nothing passed the ward gate after dark.
The mistress of the house has not been seen or heard since the first week.
Eight or nine empty jars stacked in the courtyard: squat, grey, wrong at the neck, sealed with waxed cord in a knot Xu Ping does not know. Not a vessel used in this city.
Flagstones washed and steaming at the second drum of a winter night.
At dusk the house smells of musk, mugwort smoke, pine, and beneath those a green, cold, bitter smell Xu Ping cannot name.
The green is strongest in the waste water leaving the east gutter, and the water is warm.

In his last two months Geng Su grew thin, stopped riding, and left the ward five or six times before the dawn drum. He returned before the household woke, once carrying something wrapped and heavy, wet to the ankle.
